criteria: Preserve visually distinct neutral macro-phenotypes without requiring every subdivision to define a new macroregion.
Separate blank, background, and section-edge appearances from pale low-cellularity tissue.
Retain cellular variation reproduced across anonymized Slides A-D, assessed using centroid, per-slide, mid/random, and low-margin exemplars together with anonymous spatial maps and composition plots.
metadata.review_scope: Blinded technical visual review of candidate K=3 through K=9 using only the anonymized exemplar atlases, spatial heatmaps, composition plots, lineage/summary visuals, and internal candidate metrics supplied for this run.
metadata.blinding_limitation: Only anonymized run materials were reviewed. This is a technical non-pathologist assessment based on neutral visual morphology and is not a diagnostic interpretation.

candidates.qualitative_notes: C0 is a dense cohesive purple cellular class represented on Slides A-D. C1 is a second cellular class with more blank gaps, interfaces, and heterogeneous texture. C2 pools clearly different appearances in one class: nearly blank background fields, a fibre-like foreign artefact, narrow sparse strand/boundary fragments, and pale pink amorphous granular low-nuclear material; its centroid, per-slide, and mid/random examples move between these appearances. Blank/background, sparse boundary strands, and pale amorphous material are therefore not preserved as separate neutral macro-phenotypes.

C0 and C1 keep two reproducible cellular appearances across Slides A-D, and C2 isolates narrow sparse strand-and-boundary fragments with scattered nuclei. However, C3 still pools nearly blank fields with isolated specks together with pale pink amorphous granular material and loose sparse tissue in its centroid, per-slide, and mid/random examples. The principal near-background versus pale amorphous low-nuclear-material distinction remains merged, so the macro-phenotype separation is not yet preserved.

K=5 separates the three non-cellular appearances that earlier candidates merged: C2 is a coherent pale pink amorphous granular low-nuclear-material class, concentrated in one large contiguous region on Slide C with smaller coherent patches on Slide D, essentially absent from Slide A and minimal on Slide B; C3 is narrow sparse strand/boundary tissue with scattered nuclei occurring as thin rims on all four slides; and C4 is near-blank background with isolated specks and edge fragments. C0 remains a dense cohesive cellular class and C1 a heterogeneous cellular class with gaps and interfaces, both represented on Slides A-D. The anonymous spatial maps show contiguous coherent regions rather than speckle for every class.

The pale amorphous material (C3), sparse strand/boundary tissue (C4), and near-blank background (C5) remain separated as at K=5. The additional class subdivides the cellular compartment into a dense cohesive class (C0), a darker, more tightly packed cellular class (C1), and a cellular-with-gaps boundary-adjacent class (C2). The pale amorphous class narrows to coherent regions on Slides C and D only. No previously separated macro-phenotype is re-merged, and no class pools clearly different appearances.

All distinctions from K=5/K=6 persist: pale amorphous granular material (C4, Slides C and D), sparse strand/boundary tissue (C5), and near-blank background (C6) stay separate. The extra classes further subdivide cellular tissue, adding a spindled/streaming interface appearance (C2) beside the dense (C0/C1) and gap-containing (C3) cellular classes. This is a subdivision of existing macro-phenotypes rather than the recovery of a new one.

Macro-phenotype separation is retained; the background compartment now splits into a uniformly blank class (C5) and a blank-with-specks/edge-fragment class (C7), alongside the sparse strand class (C6) and the pale amorphous class (C4, Slides C and D). Cellular tissue is divided into four related appearances (C0-C3). The additional classes are subdivisions of already separated phenotypes; visually this K adds granularity without merging.

All macro-phenotypes remain separated (pale amorphous C5 on Slides C and D; loose spindled tissue C4; strand/boundary C7; uniformly blank C6; blank-with-specks C8). The cellular compartment is again subdivided (C0-C3). As at K=7 and K=8, the additional classes refine existing appearances rather than exposing a new reproducible macro-phenotype.
